history.dynasty: Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) era; present structure attributed to Maratha chief Sadashivrao Bhau (c. 1760)
history.period: Ancient (mythological antiquity claimed); early-medieval to 18th-century fabric
history.summary: One of Kurukshetra's most revered Shiva shrines. Legend holds that Brahma himself established the first Shiva lingam here, that Shiva was first worshipped in linga form at this spot, and that the Pandavas with Krishna prayed here before the Mahabharata battle for victory. Ancient Sthaneshwar (Thanesar) was the capital of Emperor Harshavardhana of the Pushyabhuti dynasty, which took its name from the Sthaneshwar Shiva. The Vamana Purana mentions the site's sanctity; local tradition says Parashurama slew the Kshatriyas here and that the temple tank's water healed King Ban of leprosy. The present temple is said to have been built by Sadashivrao Bhau, Maratha commander-in-chief, to commemorate his victory over Ahmad Shah Abdali at Kunjpura before the third battle of Panipat. A large blue Shiva idol rests on a stone slab in the centre of the temple tank. Tradition holds that no Kurukshetra pilgrimage is complete without visiting this temple.

name: Sthaneshwar Mahadev Temple
town_description: Thanesar (ancient Sthanishvara) is the old temple town that grew around the Sthaneshwar Mahadev shrine; it was the capital of the Pushyabhuti dynasty under Emperor Harshavardhana in the early 7th century CE. Today it forms the core of the Kurukshetra urban agglomeration on the Grand Trunk Road in Haryana, anchoring the 48-kos Kurukshetra pilgrimage circuit with Brahma Sarovar, the Shaktipeeth, and the Mahabharata battlefield sites. The town draws pilgrims year-round and is busiest during Gita Jayanti, solar-eclipse fairs, and Maha Shivaratri.
